judicial_history.date_conflict: The primary appellate opinion at PDF page 6 cites Dkt. 57, Order of August 24, 2018. The held Presidential memorandum describes an August 25 injunction, matching the opinion date. The actual order is required.
judicial_history.mandate_evidence: Actual court-authored one-page mandate read at university mirror (CADCMANDATE2019_MIRROR), matching OPM October 4, 2019 p1 and 73 FLRA No.96 fn8. Native retention and official court custody remain open.
judicial_history.distinction: The injunction constrained implementation of specified provisions. It did not abolish the orders or their unaffected commands. The mandate restored implementation; protected CBAs continued to limit applications.
judicial_history.procedural_character: The injunction was part of a final summary judgment, not merely a preliminary order. Its operative duration was limited by later appellate vacatur for lack of jurisdiction.

first_cessation_policy: A temporary injunction is a suspension episode, not permanent legal extinction. Exact first suspension date remains August24–25 2018 pending Dkt57; July16 appellate decision is distinct from October3 mandate. A one-off task can be exhausted by actual performance before formal revocation; composite scopes retain separate component dates.
review_scope: Producer proposal; approved=false. Native frozen evidence has not been supplemented or assembled. No independent or human approval.
residual_effects_through_cutoff: No automatic revival inferred from EO14148 revoking EO14003/14029. Existing CBA terms, statutory authorities, regulatory proceedings and litigation require their own legal bases and endpoints. Evidence establishes particular surviving consequences after revocation, not an exhaustive cutoff-wide residual-effects inventory.
